title: Additivity of complexity under products
statement:
Let $p_1$ be a finite-message protocol over inputs $X_1$, $Y_1$ with outputs in $\alpha_1$, and let $p_2$ be a finite-message protocol over inputs $X_2$, $Y_2$ with outputs in $\alpha_2$. Then the communication complexity of their product protocol, which runs $p_1$ on the first input components and $p_2$ on the second and pairs the two outputs, equals the sum of their individual complexities:
\[
  \mathrm{complexity}(p_1 \times p_2) \;=\; \mathrm{complexity}(p_1) + \mathrm{complexity}(p_2).
\]
hypotheses_covered: p1 is a finite-message protocol over X1, Y1, α1
p2 is a finite-message protocol over X2, Y2, α2
replaced:
The complexity of the product protocol satisfies
\[
  (p_1.\texttt{prod}\;p_2).\texttt{complexity}
  \;=\; p_1.\texttt{complexity} + p_2.\texttt{complexity}.
\]
